credit: Anointed Staff original practice scripts. Desk-safe spiritual disciplines framed by Scripture — not a third-party ascension list. Spoken guides: /audio/practice (ElevenLabs · River).
stance: Practice these as quiet disciplines beside the Word. They are not magic, not fortune, and not medical advice. Sun-gazing, astral travel, and occult contract language are refused on this desk.

sessions.title: Whole-body breath
steps: Sit or stand where you can be still. Place one hand on the belly.
Breathe in slowly so the belly rises first — as a child breathes — then let the breath fill the chest without strain.
On the out-breath, thank the Giver of breath (Genesis 2:7). Imagine nothing fancy; simply receive air as gift.
Continue for the timer. If the mind wanders, return to the next breath and the Name who gives it.

sessions.title: Rejoice and laugh
steps: Recall one true kindness or absurd mercy from this week — not forced positivity.
Let a real smile or laugh loosen the jaw and chest (Philippians 4:4).
Say aloud or silently: Rejoice in the Lord — then breathe once more in that lightness.
End by naming one person you can encourage today.

sessions.title: Read the Word slowly
steps: Open the Bible window to a short passage (Psalm 19, Psalm 119, or the chapter already on the desk).
Read one verse aloud. Pause. Read it again under your breath.
Ask: What does this show of the Lord’s character? Write one line in Notes if you wish.
Close with: Your word is a lamp to my feet (Psalm 119:105).

sessions.title: Walk in creation
steps: If you can, step outside or to a window. Feel feet on solid ground or floor.
Look at sky, tree, or light for one unhurried minute without a phone (Psalm 19:1).
Name three created things you see and thank their Maker — not the things as gods.
Return indoors settled; open Heavens → Circle if you want the same glory framed as study clocks.

sessions.title: Fasting frame (short)
steps: This session prepares a fast; it does not force hunger. If health forbids fasting, stop and pray only.
Choose one meal or snack you will set aside for prayer later today (Matthew 6:16–18).
Ask the Lord what hunger should point to — Scripture, not self-display.
When the timer ends, write the commitment in Notes → Write.

sessions.title: Psalm tone
steps: Choose a short line: Let every thing that hath breath praise the Lord (Psalm 150:6), or Holy, holy, holy.
Hum or speak the line on one gentle tone for a few breaths — prayer, not a technique sold as vibration magic.
If speech is hard, intone the words silently with the same intention.
Finish in quiet, then open a psalm in the Bible window.
